# File uploads and attachment validation

> Loaded when you touch `backend/app/services/attachment_validation.py`, `backend/app/api/v1/card_logos.py`, `backend/app/api/v1/file_attachments.py`, `backend/app/api/v1/resources.py`, … (full list in the frontmatter). Moved verbatim from `CLAUDE.md`; edit it here.

- **An upload is what its bytes say, not what the client calls it.** Every attachment-style upload goes through `services/attachment_upload.py` (`read_validated_upload`: format from the name, bounded read, content check; `require_uploads_enabled`; `content_disposition`) — card attachments, decision files — and extension-owned resources through `resource_service.validate_file_upload`, which calls the same `validate_attachment`; never a route-local MIME allowlist. `file.content_type` is multipart metadata the client writes, so it decides nothing: `backend/app/services/attachment_validation.py` resolves the **extension** to a format, requires the leading bytes to prove the container, and stores that table's **canonical** MIME — never the browser's string, which is how `image/jpg` and `application/x-zip-compressed` used to split one format into two Resources filter rows. A signature identifies a container, not a format (every OOXML and ODF file is a zip; `.doc`/`.xls`/`.ppt`/`.msg` are all OLE2), so the extension tells family members apart and the signature is what stops a renamed executable — that is the honest limit of the check. The size cap (`MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`, 20 MB) lives there too and is mirrored in **three** other places that must not drift: the edge nginx's `client_max_body_size` (deliberately *higher*, see below), `frontend/src/lib/attachmentFormats.ts` (the `accept=` list, the pre-upload checks and the filter sidebar all derive from it) and the manual (the manual is not checked by the test). `tests/services/test_upload_limits.py` reads the Dockerfile's `client_max_body_size` and the TS mirror off disk (and, for the 2 GB workspace bundle, the chart and Terraform ingress manifests) and fails on any disagreement — written because the last drift (nginx 5 MB vs. an advertised 10 MB) shipped a raw 413 to users and no test noticed. `card_logos.sniff_image_mime` is the same posture for card logos; `services` must not import from `api`, so the four image signatures are deliberately duplicated. Read-scope and extension-entity 404s on these routes: see card-read-scope.md. Guard tests: `tests/services/test_attachment_validation.py`, `tests/api/test_file_attachments.py`.
